summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 2,290 Cr, but EBITDA margin fell 272 bps to 15.7% on SPECT supply shortfall and Montreal under-absorption.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 19% YoY to Rs 2,290 Cr on radiopharma, allergy immunotherapy, CDMO sterile injectables and generics, while EBITDA rose only 2% to Rs 363 Cr. Normalized PAT was Rs 129 Cr, down YoY on higher depreciation and interest. For FY26, revenue grew 14% to Rs 8,280 Cr, EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 1,326 Cr and margin fell 99 bps to 15.9%, mainly from lower CMO Montreal output in H2. Management frames FY27 margins as a two-half story, with H1 hit by SPECT shortages and H2 expected at 17-18%.

segments.name: Radiopharma
segments.commentary: Q4 growth was driven by radiopharma but SPECT cold kit shortage (Montreal-linked) cut high-margin sales; management expects about $14 million SPECT revenue impact in H1 FY27. Ruby-Fill market growing about 10% with franchise growth guided at 30%+.

segments.name: CDMO Sterile Injectables (Spokane)
segments.commentary: Line 3 has 10+ products in tech transfer, about 80% complex biologics, with commercial production from late FY27 subject to FDA approval; peak revenue for Line 3 targeted at $80-90 million. Line 3 tech transfer revenue of $60-80 million expected in FY27.

segments.name: CMO Montreal
segments.commentary: Under-absorption and lower production hit margins; FY26 loss including exceptionals was about Rs 200 Cr and FY27 is expected to look similar. Line 5 revenue expected from FY29 after media fills.

segments.name: API / Custom manufacturing
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin maintained at about 15%; innovator custom manufacturing revenue expected to start contributing in FY27. Innovator clients not named due to confidentiality.

segments.name: Discovery (CRO)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 15% to above Rs 650 Cr with margin growth; management flagged near-term competitive intensity in large pharma.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 13% and EBITDA margin moved into double digits; target close to 15% margin going forward.

segments.name: Allergy immunotherapy
segments.commentary: About 90% of sales are US and 8-10% non-US. Management said FY26 growth was 12%, with US growing 3-5% and non-US volume gains driving growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated growth guided at low double digits, with margins in the 38-40% range (per Harsher Singh; this appears to be a segment-level margin reference, not consolidated EBITDA).
EBITDA margin is a two-half story: H1 FY27 temporarily lower on SPECT shortage; H2 FY27 margins of 17-18% as Montreal stabilizes, which is expected to represent the FY28 run-rate.
SPECT supply expected to be released mid to end Q2 FY27, with Q3 and Q4 returning to regular run rate.
MIBG full NDA filing targeted for H2 FY27, with accelerated review (about six months) given orphan drug status; company intends to launch in-house.
Net debt targeted at zero by FY2030; net debt reduction expected from FY2028 onward.
Tax rate around 33% currently, expected to decline as PBT grows with Line 3 and Line 4 margin gains.
No capex beyond Line 3, Line 4, Line 5 and PET manufacturing expected over the next 12-18 months (per Priyavrat Bhartia).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex expected similar to FY26 capex of Rs 1,668 Cr.
Spokane Line 4: nearly $200 million spent, about $34 million remaining. Line 3 commercial production from late FY27.
Montreal Line 5: $27 million spent, $87 million pending; revenue from FY29 after media fills.
PET pharmacies: $22 million spent, $50 million pending; first three expected to commercialize in FY27, with some possibly slipping, subject to FDA PAI.
Cyclotrons being contracted; new PET sites typically take 3-4 years to reach peak based on peer ramps.
demand_pricing: Line 3 products are largely complex biologics, where management says it commands price premiums and high switching costs; one of the world's largest oncology products onboarded on Line 3.
Ruby-Fill market growing about 10%, with Jubilant gaining share and pricing momentum in the US; razor-blade model with generator deliveries every 6-7 weeks.
Discovery: management expects biotech demand to improve on patent-cliff-driven funding, while large pharma faces more competition.
Allergy US market growing about 3-5%; company gaining share there. Non-US (Europe) share is low and is a growth focus.
Generics margin reached double digits; company guides to close to 15% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Line 3 pipeline: biologics vs small molecules, and when commercials start?
qa_highlights.answer: 10+ products in tech transfer, about 80% complex biologics; commercial production from late FY27 subject to FDA approval; peak revenue of $80-90 million, 1.5-2 years earlier than projected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H1 FY27 radiopharma cost pressure and what changes in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: SPECT cold kit stock constrained, released mid to end Q2 FY27; H1 SPECT revenue impact about $14 million at high margins; H2 returns to regular run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Has the API business onboarded innovator clients and when will revenue come?
qa_highlights.answer: Innovator names and count not disclosed under confidentiality; custom manufacturing revenue expected to kick in FY27, with EBITDA margin held at about 15% now and rising over the short to medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Montreal loss trajectory and path to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 loss about Rs 200 Cr including exceptionals; FY27 similar; meaningful reduction in FY28 via cost cuts; no breakeven guidance for FY29. Revenue recognition is on sell-through basis.

qa_highlights.question: MIBG filing timing, approval path, and FY28 radiopharma outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Full NDA filing in H2 FY27, accelerated review possible; one FY27 product pulled out and pipeline moved to third-party CMOs; FY28 expected to normalize SPECT, Ruby-Fill growing 30%+, and NDA launch years to carry sales and marketing investment.

qa_highlights.question: Capital structure, capex, and deleveraging?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex Rs 1,668 Cr, FY27 similar; net debt Rs 1,952 Cr, targeted to reach zero by FY2030 with reduction from FY28 as Line 3 and 4 cash flows come through.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate outlook and PET pharmacy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax rate about 33% with unshielded expenses pushing it higher; to decline as PBT grows. First three PET pharmacies expected to commercialize in FY27, with possible slippage.

risks_watch: SPECT cold kit supply: any slip beyond mid-to-end Q2 FY27 would extend the H1 margin hit.
MIBG NDA filing in H2 FY27; full NDA rather than 505(b)(2), and PRV eligibility uncertain given the discontinued Azedra approval.
Line 3 commercial start late FY27 depends on FDA approval of 10+ products; Line 3 peak timelines hinge on that.
Montreal losses (about Rs 200 Cr in FY26) expected to repeat in FY27; sell-through booking adds revenue timing uncertainty.
Net debt of Rs 1,952 Cr and the FY30 zero net debt target; PET pharmacy FDA inspection timing may slip.
Discovery large-pharma competition; Line 5 revenue not until FY29.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth (Line 3 peak revenue, Ruby-Fill, net debt zero by FY30) but cautious on near-term margins, with H1 FY27 weakness openly flagged. Management was evasive on several specifics, declining to disclose Montreal revenue share, innovator client names, European allergy market size, and FY28/FY29 numeric guidance.
key_quotes: As production at CMO Montreal stabilizes, we expect EBITDA margin to start strengthening from H2 FY2027 onwards.
In terms of EBITDA margin, it shall be the story of two halves.
we are committed to achieve net debt zero by 2030.
we expect to launch this product ourselves.

Montreal Line 5 ($27M spent, $87M pending; revenue from FY29 after media fills)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue growth to low double digits (taken as ~10%) and H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 17-18%, backed by Spokane Line 3 tech transfer revenue of $60-80M in FY27 and Line 3 commercial production from late FY27, though the SPECT shortage hits H1 FY27 and Montreal losses are expected to repeat.
